chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who owns a blood relative: is it proper for him to sell him or enslave him?

He عليه السلام said: It is not proper for him to sell him, nor may he take him as a slave. He is his mawla and his brother in religion. Whichever of the two dies, the other inherits from him, unless he has an heir closer to him than the other.

key_terms.ذَا رَحِمِهِ: a blood relative or close kin
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his mawla, one bound to him through wala'
key_terms.وَارِثٌ أَقْرَبُ: a nearer heir with stronger inheritance priority
key_terms.يَسْتَعْبِدَهُ: to enslave him or take him as a slave

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell or enslave a relative whom he owns in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ownership of a close blood relative, stating that such a person may not be sold or kept as a slave. It also affirms a bond of wala' and religious brotherhood between them, with inheritance applying between them when no closer heir exists.
